thread:
kyle: quick question — running into a chart templating quirk during a prod deploy. we have a values-driven envFrom that looks like this in the template:

```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.service.secretName | default "" }}
```

when secretName is not set the rendered manifest ends up with `name: ""` which k8s rejects. we tried `--values=prod.yaml` + `--set service.secretName=` and it still renders empty string. what’s the cleanest helm pattern to *omit* the whole envFrom block when secretName is absent (and keep it when present)? also any gotchas when external-secrets is creating that secret asynchronously?


 tanya: short answer: guard the block with an if. i usually do:

```gotemplate
{{- if .Values.service.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.service.secretName }}
{{- end }}
```

that prevents `name: ""`. avoid `default ""` here — default is what causes empty string rendering.

 arjun: also watch indentation if you use `toYaml` or `include` templates. example pattern i like for optional blocks:

```gotemplate
{{- with .Values.service.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ . }}
{{- end }}
```

`with` is handy because it makes `.` the value.

 sam: if you need to support both a literal secret and an external secrets ref, do an explicit conditional for both. e.g. check `externalSecret.enabled` first, otherwise fall back to `service.secretName`. something like:

```gotemplate
{{- if .Values.externalSecret.enabled }}
# rely on ExternalSecret creating k8s Secret, nothing to render here (maybe annotations)
{{- else if .Values.service.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.service.secretName }}
{{- end }}
```

 this avoids rendering a blank name when the external secret path is empty.

 kyle: nice — quick followups: 1) is there any case where `--set service.secretName=` (empty) vs omitting the `--set` changes how `with` behaves? 2) our CI linter (helm lint) still passes even when manifest has `name: ""`, but k8s apply fails. want to catch it earlier in CI.

 tanya: 1) if you `--set service.secretName=` that sets it to empty string which is truthy for template existence checks? actually empty strings are falsy in `if`/`with`, so `with` will not run. but `default ""` will return empty string and cause rendering — so avoid default when you want to omit.

 2) for CI, add a chart test that renders manifests and asserts `name: ""` does not appear, or run `helm template` and `grep -q '\bname: ""'` (fail on match). small example:

```bash
helm template ./mychart -f ci-values.yaml | grep -E 'name:\s*""' && exit 1 || true
```

 sam: another lint trick: `kubeval` will catch invalid k8s objects. combine `helm template` + `kubeval` in pipeline. also `yamllint`/`kube-linter` are useful.

 arjun: on the external-secrets timing — if ExternalSecret creates the secret asynchronously you can: 1) ensure rollout waits for secret existence via `initContainer` that blocks until secret exists, or 2) leverage `external-secrets` `syncPolicy` to create before application, or 3) add `kubectl wait` step in infra apply. note: avoiding rendering a secretRef that points to a non-existent secret still yields a pod that may fail to start; handle with retries or pre-provision.

 kyle: perfect. i'll update chart with `with` guard + add helm template grep in CI. will also open a follow-up PR to add kubeval in the lint job. thanks! :thumbsup:

 deploy-bot: CI: helm/chart-myservice#123 — template step failed checks? actually passed (no name: ""). full lint job: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345

 kyle: tagging @tanya @sam for review on the PR once i have changes in branch `fix/helm-optional-secret`

 tanya: ack, will review this morning.

 sam: +1, also mention docs on the chart README about the secret contract so infra knows expected behavior.

 kyle: good call — adding a short snippet in README and an example prod values.
